methodological_rigor.justification: Single-institution retrospective cohort of 25 patients with liver-limited metastatic SCCA treated over three decades (1993-2023) at Mayo Clinic, identified through a prospectively maintained ATE database. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are clear, outcome definitions (OS, DFS) are standard and defined from liver-directed therapy date. Kaplan-Meier estimation and univariate Cox are appropriate. Major limitations: very small sample precludes multivariable modeling (authors acknowledge), substantial selection bias toward favorable biology (patients progressing on chemotherapy were not offered metastasectomy), 30-year accrual spans major practice shifts (including pre- and post-immunotherapy eras), and median follow-up (22 months) is short relative to the reported median OS of 51.3 months, limiting precision of OS estimates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses a genuine clinical gap: there is no standard-of-care for liver-limited metastatic SCCA, and existing evidence is restricted to small series. Median OS of 51.3 months — substantially exceeding historical systemic-therapy outcomes (~20-29 months) — provides useful hypothesis-generating data supporting liver-directed therapy in selected patients and informs multidisciplinary decision-making. Classified Oxford LoE 4 as a small retrospective single-center case series.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to this observational cohort. Most items (setting, participants, variable definitions, IRB approval with number, statistical methods, limitations) are covered. Tables and figures are referenced but not fully summarized in text. Gaps include: no explicit STROBE checklist appendix, no flow diagram of patient identification/exclusion, limited baseline characteristics reported in extracted text (full detail deferred to Table 1), no data/code availability statement, and some redundancy between results and discussion. Minor typo ('dichotimized'). Scored 3 overall.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper is one of the largest single-institution series on liver metastasectomy for SCCA (authors so claim), extending prior reports (Pawlik et al. multi-institutional, Goldner et al. NCDB, Lo et al., Rogers et al., and Hurt et al. systematic review) with 30-year Mayo Clinic experience. The observed median OS is longer than in most prior series, which is notable. Extension of prior work rather than a novel methodological or therapeutic advance; however, the integration of emerging topics (ctDNA, HPV biology) in Discussion adds some depth. Score 3 for meaningful extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, well-organized, and appropriately cautious about selection bias. The Discussion engages substantively with adjacent literature (InterAACT, InterAACT-2/POD1UM-303, Pawlik, Rogers, Hurt), and future directions (ctDNA, SBRT) are thoughtfully raised. Limitations are transparent. Minor issues: typo ('dichotimized'), some repetitive phrasing ('liver-directed therapy' restated multiple times), and heavy reliance on narrative description of tables/figures not fully reproduced in the extracted text. Overall polished.

key_strengths: One of the largest single-institution series of curative-intent hepatic-directed therapy for liver-limited metastatic SCCA (n=25 over 30 years)
Detailed reporting of preoperative response, resection extent, margin status, and recurrence patterns
Median OS of 51.3 months substantially exceeds systemic-therapy-only benchmarks (InterAACT 20 months; InterAACT-2 29.2 months)
Transparent acknowledgment of selection bias toward favorable disease biology and the limitations of small sample size
Thoughtful discussion of emerging tools (ctDNA, HPV-specific assays, SBRT) for future refinement of patient selection
key_concerns: Very small sample size (n=25) precludes multivariable modeling and limits subgroup conclusions
30-year accrual spans major changes in systemic therapy (pre- and post-immunotherapy); heterogeneity not formally addressed
Median follow-up (22 months) is notably shorter than median OS (51.3 months), suggesting unstable survival estimates
Strong selection bias: patients were only offered local therapy if chemosensitive; generalizability to broader oligometastatic population is limited
No flow diagram; incomplete data availability statement
Recurrence rate (80%) remains very high despite favorable OS, underscoring uncertainty about true long-term cure
chief_reviewer.rationale: Carefully framed and well-written single-center retrospective series on a rare clinical question; hypothesis-generating for liver-directed therapy in SCCA. Appropriate for a tier-3 GI-oncology or surgical-oncology journal after minor revisions to add a flow diagram and more explicit discussion of accrual-era heterogeneity.
